description:
What If a Gamma-Ray Burst Hit Earth?

Episode 56 of a daily journey through the universe. 💥
Gamma-ray bursts: in seconds they can release more energy than our Sun will in its whole lifetime. Discovered by accident by spy satellites in the 1960s. In October 2022, the brightest one ever seen hit Earth's upper atmosphere from about 2 billion light-years away.

segments.text: What if the biggest explosion since the Big Bang went off near Earth?
In the nineteen sixties, the United States launched satellites to watch for secret nuclear bomb tests.
segments.headline: Spy satellites

segments.text: They caught flashes of gamma rays, the most powerful kind of light. But they weren't coming from Earth. They were coming from space.
segments.headline: Flashes from space

segments.text: In just seconds, a gamma-ray burst can release more energy than our Sun will in its entire ten-billion-year life.

visual.label: more energy than the Sun's whole life

segments.text: The longer ones happen when a giant star collapses into a black hole, shooting two narrow jets out at nearly the speed of light.
segments.headline: A dying giant star

segments.text: The shorter ones happen when two neutron stars crash together, the same collisions that make gold.
segments.headline: Neutron stars colliding

segments.text: In October twenty twenty-two, the brightest burst ever recorded hit Earth. Astronomers nicknamed it the BOAT: the brightest of all time.
segments.headline: The BOAT, 2022

segments.text: It came from about two billion light-years away, and it still disturbed Earth's upper atmosphere.
Some scientists have suggested a nearby burst could have contributed to a mass extinction on Earth, about four hundred forty million years ago. It's an idea, not proven.
segments.headline: A danger? Maybe once

segments.text: Don't worry. No star close enough to hurt us is known to be about to do this.
segments.headline: We're safe
